input.newString:
[[ "$(<"$HOME/.bashrc")" == *"$expected_hook"* ]] || fail "managed Bash configuration must enable direnv"
  HOME="$original_home"
}

# The PATH tests below all mutate $HOME and $PATH of this very process, so each
# one takes a sandbox of its own and every caller restores both afterwards.
# ensure_shell_configuration creates $HOME/.local/bin itself; the other two
# managed directories are created by whichever test wants them to exist.
setup_path_sandbox() {
  local sandbox="$TEMP_DIR/$1"

  HOME="$sandbox/home"
  DRY_RUN=0
  mkdir -p "$HOME"
}

# Prints the body of the managed block written into ~/.bashrc. What a fresh
# shell runs is that emitted text, not the installer's own functions, so the
# block has to be exercised as the standalone Bash it becomes.
extract_managed_bash_block() {
  awk -v start='# >>> agentic-dev-toolkit >>>' -v end='# <<< agentic-dev-toolkit <<<' '
    $0 == end   { inside = 0 }
    inside      { print }
    $0 == start { inside = 1 }
  ' "$1"
}

# Sources the managed block in a fresh, rc-less Bash with a controlled PATH and
# prints the resulting PATH. Sourcing it twice is the point: a login shell that
# has already run ~/.bashrc must not gain a second copy of anything.
run_managed_bash_block() {
  local home="$1" starting_path="$2" times="$3"
  local block="$home/managed-block.sh"

  extract_managed_bash_block "$home/.bashrc" > "$block"

  # The block hooks direnv. A stub inside a managed directory keeps the test off
  # whatever direnv the host does or does not have, and is reachable only if the
  # block put that directory on PATH in the first place.
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" ":"\n' > "$home/.local/bin/direnv"
  chmod 755 "$home/.local/bin/direnv"

  HOME="$home" "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c '
    PATH="$2"
    for (( i = 0; i < $3; i++ )); do
      # shellcheck disable=SC1090
      source "$1"
    done
    printf "%s\n" "$PATH"
  ' _ "$block" "$starting_path" "$times"
}

test_managed_path_prepends_existing_directories_in_priority_order() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-priority
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"
  PATH="/usr/bin:/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  # .local/bin wins over ~/bin, which wins over the OpenCode shim directory:
  # this is what decides which `opencode`, `mise` or `node` a shell resolves.
  assert_equal "$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
    "newly added managed directories must keep their documented priority"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_path_skips_directories_that_do_not_exist() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-missing-dirs
  # Only $HOME/.local/bin exists, and the installer is what creates it. A
  # workstation with no ~/bin and no OpenCode shim directory must not carry two
  # dead entries on every command lookup.
  PATH="/usr/bin:/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  assert_equal "$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
    "a managed directory that does not exist must not be added to PATH"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_path_does_not_duplicate_an_entry_already_present() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-no-duplicates
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"
  # A profile that already exports ~/bin is the common case this guard exists
  # for; re-running the installer must not grow PATH each time.
  PATH="/usr/bin:$HOME/bin:/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null
  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  assert_equal "$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:/usr/bin:$HOME/bin:/bin" \
    "an entry already on PATH must be left where the user put it, exactly once"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_path_matches_complete_entries_only() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-exact-entries
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/bin/nested" "$HOME/binary" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"
  # Neither a directory *below* a managed one nor one whose name merely starts
  # with it satisfies the requirement, so a substring test would silently drop
  # ~/bin from PATH and leave the tools in it unreachable.
  PATH="$HOME/bin/nested:$HOME/binary:/usr/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  assert_equal "$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:$HOME/bin/nested:$HOME/binary:/usr/bin" \
    "only a complete, exact PATH entry counts as already present"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_path_leaves_pre_existing_entries_untouched() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-preserves-existing
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"
  # PATH order and even its duplicates are the user's, and may be load-bearing
  # for a tool shadowed on purpose. The installer prepends; it does not tidy.
  PATH="/opt/dup:/opt/dup:/usr/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  assert_equal "$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:/opt/dup:/opt/dup:/usr/bin" \
    "pre-existing entries must not be reordered, canonicalized or deduplicated"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_bash_block_is_idempotent_in_a_fresh_shell() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-bashrc-block
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  # What the user actually lives with is ~/.bashrc, re-read by every shell and
  # by `exec bash -l` after the installer's own advice. The block must reach the
  # same PATH whether it runs once or twice.
  local once twice
  once="$(run_managed_bash_block "$HOME" "/usr/bin:$HOME/bin:/bin" 1)"
  twice="$(run_managed_bash_block "$HOME" "/usr/bin:$HOME/bin:/bin" 2)"

  assert_equal "$once" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:/usr/bin:$HOME/bin:/bin" \
    "the managed block must prepend only what is missing, in priority order"
  assert_equal "$twice" "$once" \
    "re-sourcing the managed block must not add a second copy of anything"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_bash_block_skips_directories_that_do_not_exist() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-bashrc-missing
  # A directory can appear later, so the block decides per shell rather than
  # baking in what happened to exist at install time.
  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  local before after
  before="$(run_managed_bash_block "$HOME" "/usr/bin:/bin" 1)"
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
  after="$(run_managed_bash_block "$HOME" "/usr/bin:/bin" 1)"

  assert_equal "$before" "$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
    "the managed block must skip managed directories that do not exist"
  assert_equal "$after" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
    "the managed block must pick up a managed directory created after installation"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_managed_path_handles_directories_with_spaces() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox 'path with spaces'
  mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"
  PATH="/usr/bin:$HOME/bin"

  ensure_shell_configuration >/dev/null

  assert_equal "$PATH" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:/usr/bin:$HOME/bin" \
    "a home directory containing spaces must not split into separate PATH entries"

  local observed
  observed="$(run_managed_bash_block "$HOME" "/usr/bin:$HOME/bin" 2)"
  assert_equal "$observed" "$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:/usr/bin:$HOME/bin" \
    "the managed block must handle a home directory containing spaces"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_installer_bootstrap_path_skips_missing_directories() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-bootstrap
  # The installer prepends the same directories to its own PATH at startup,
  # before any function runs, and that site needs the same guard as the others.
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"

  local observed
  observed="$(HOME="$HOME" PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c '
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    source "$1"
    printf "%s\n" "$PATH"
  ' _ "$TEMP_DIR/install-functions.sh")"

  assert_equal "$observed" "$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
    "the installer bootstrap must prepend only managed directories that exist"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

test_installer_bootstrap_path_does_not_duplicate_existing_entries() {
  local original_home="$HOME" original_path="$PATH"
  setup_path_sandbox path-bootstrap-duplicates
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/.opencode/bin"

  local observed
  observed="$(HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin" "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c '
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    source "$1"
    printf "%s\n" "$PATH"
  ' _ "$TEMP_DIR/install-functions.sh")"

  assert_equal "$observed" "$HOME/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin" \
    "the installer bootstrap must not duplicate directories the environment already provides"

  HOME="$original_home"
  PATH="$original_path"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Test-harness helper (outside the workspace): run a single test from
# tests/install.sh so each new test can be watched fail and pass on its own.
set -Eeuo pipefail
suite="/tmp/opencode/path-eval-b/tests/install.sh"
for name in "$@"; do
  driver="$(mktemp /tmp/opencode/one-test-XXXXXX.sh)"
  awk '/^TEMP_DIR="\$\(mktemp -d\)"$/ { print; exit } { print }' "$suite" > "$driver"
  printf 'load_installer_functions\n%s\nprintf "PASS: %s\\n"\n' "$name" "$name" >> "$driver"
  printf -- '--- %s\n' "$name"
  setsid bash "$driver" < /dev/null || printf 'EXIT=%s\n' "$?"
  rm -f "$driver"
done
